quotes.text: Most people think triggers are simple switches, but triggers are ears, they hear everything, you must teach them to ignore, guardrails are not decoration.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes triggers as the main risk surface of a flow and motivates trigger conditions.

quotes.text: Retry is not hope, it's math, exponential back off, ceiling, circuit breaker, three tries for network flinch, one for a hard 403, if the breaker opens, you don't keep knocking.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Turns retry handling into a concrete, defensible rule set.

quotes.text: A flow that depends on a person is a candle in a draft, a flow that depends on a principle is a lantern bolted to stone.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable argument for binding connections to service principals instead of people.

quotes.text: These patterns don't make you safe, they make you ready, the orchestrator respects only structure, give it names, give it gates, give it records that outlive you.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Sums up the episode's thesis that structure, not tooling, makes automation reliable.

quotes.text: Excel as a trigger, never, Excel remembers and it punishes, files lock, rows shift, tables break when someone fixes formatting.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear, actionable anti-pattern warning for flow builders.

takeaways: Triggers are the riskiest part of a flow, so gate them with trigger conditions, pre-filters and server-side queries and keep concurrency off until you own a partition key.
Reliable flows follow one scaffold everywhere: try, catch and finally scopes, append-only logging with correlation IDs, named terminations, bounded retries with circuit breakers and a poison queue.
Architect automation as a master orchestrator with light task routers and small idempotent child flows, owned by service principals and governed by DLP, environments and regular owner sweeps.
hook: Power Automate flows that start as quick wins often end as runaway loops, orphaned approvals and 3 a.m. throttling storms nobody can trace. This episode is for makers, admins and architects who own automation in Microsoft 365 and want the patterns that actually return when called: guarded triggers, try-catch scaffolds, retries with circuit breakers, child flows and a governed orchestrator blueprint.
